questions.stem: According to the passage, what causes a lunar eclipse?
options: The moon blocks light from the sun, creating a shadow on Earth
Earth is positioned between the sun and moon, casting a shadow on the moon
The moon moves closer to Earth than usual
Sunlight bends around the moon's atmosphere
questions.evidence: A lunar eclipse happens when the sun, Earth, and moon line up just right, with Earth positioned between the sun and moon.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문에서 지구가 태양과 달 사이에 위치하여 달에 그림자를 만든다고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.stem: According to the passage, all of the following are true about this eclipse EXCEPT:
options: It will be best seen in North and South America
It will last about one hour
Special equipment will be needed to view it
The moon will appear reddish-orange
questions.evidence: No special equipment will be needed to see the reddish moon.
questions.explanation_ko: 본문은 특별한 장비가 필요 없다고 말하므로, '필요하다'는 진술은 사실이 아닙니다.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about people in Europe and Africa regarding this eclipse?
options: They will not be able to see any part of the eclipse
They may see only a brief and less complete view because the moon will be near setting
They will see the eclipse better than people in the Americas
They will need to wait until March 2026 to see any eclipse
questions.evidence: The total lunar eclipse may be harder to see in Europe and Africa because the moon will be close to setting.
questions.explanation_ko: 달이 지평선 근처에 있어 보기 어렵다는 내용에서 유럽과 아프리카는 짧고 불완전한 관측만 가능할 것이라고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: In the sentence "with Earth positioned between the sun and moon," the word "positioned" most nearly means:
options: moved quickly
located or placed
hidden from view
connected
questions.evidence: A lunar eclipse happens when the sun, Earth, and moon line up just right, with Earth positioned between the sun and moon.
questions.explanation_ko: 'positioned'은 '위치해 있다'는 뜻으로, 여기서는 지구가 태양과 달 사이에 놓여 있음을 의미합니다.

questions.stem: Why does the author mention Aristotle's observation of the Earth's shadow during a lunar eclipse?
options: To show that ancient Greeks invented the concept of eclipses
To illustrate how lunar eclipses historically helped people understand the natural world, such as proving Earth is round
To compare Greek astronomy with modern NASA research
To explain why total lunar eclipses are rare
questions.evidence: The ancient Greek thinker and writer Aristotle observed that Earths’ shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse was always curved.
questions.explanation_ko: 저자는 아리스토텔레스의 관찰이 지구가 둥글다는 것을 증명하는 데 사용되었음을 보여주기 위해 이 예시를 언급합니다.

blanks.sentence_ko: 태양, 지구, 달이 정확히 일직선으로 정렬될 때 월식이 일어난다.

blanks.meaning: 붉은 달(개기월식 때 붉게 보이는 달)

blanks.sentence_ko: 지구가 태양과 달 사이에 위치하면서 이러한 현상이 일어난다.
달이 지기 직전이기 때문에 유럽과 아프리카에서는 개기월식을 보기 더 어려울 수 있다.
그것은 달을 구리와 비슷한 불그스름한 주황색으로 보이게 만든다.

key_points: A total lunar eclipse occurs when Earth is positioned between the sun and moon, casting a shadow on the moon.
The eclipse will be best visible in North and South America, with brief views possible in parts of Africa and Europe.
The eclipse, called a 'blood moon,' makes the moon appear reddish-orange due to sunlight passing through Earth's atmosphere.
The eclipse will last about one hour starting early Friday morning, with totality around 3 a.m. EDT.
Historically, civilizations used lunar eclipses to learn about celestial behavior, including Aristotle's proof that Earth is round.
The next total lunar eclipses will occur in September (visible in Asia, Africa, Australia, Europe) and March 2026 (visible in the Americas).
main_idea: A total lunar eclipse, known as a blood moon, will be visible mainly in the Americas this week, and such eclipses have long helped humans understand the sun, moon, and Earth's shape.
restate_sentence: A lunar eclipse happens when the sun, Earth, and moon line up just right, with Earth positioned between the sun and moon.
